chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Marzuban ibn Imran, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I rise [for prayer] when the dawn has broken. If I begin with the dawn prayer, I pray it at the beginning of its time; and if I begin with the night prayer and the Witr, I pray the dawn prayer during the time of these [night prayers].' He said: 'Begin with the night prayer and the Witr, and do not make that a habit.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order of prayer if one wakes up after dawn has already broken?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the preferred order of prayers for one who wakes after Fajr has entered but before the sun rises, advising the performance of Salat al-Layl and Witr first to preserve the virtue of night worship. The key scholarly nuance lies in the phrase 'do not make it a habit' (la taj'al dhalika adatan), which warns against making this specific sequence a permanent, rigid routine that might lead to neglecting the Fajr prayer in its optimal time or causing spiritual complacency. This reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing voluntary night prayers with the timely fulfillment of obligatory duties.
